To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed fuzzy logic control based battery energy management in the hybrid renewable energy source based micro grid system is effective in terms of power quality, power factor, and power management.
the proposed FLC based battery energy management is more efficient and effective compared to the conventional battery energy management system.
the FLC based MPPT algorithm is more effective in tracking maximum power point compared to conventional P&P algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a fuzzy logic controller based battery energy management for the hybrid renewable microgrid system.
a novel battery energy storage management system for hybrid solar/wind energy system.
the design and development of a fuzzy logic based bidirectional DC-DC converter for the battery energy management system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is the first of its kind in the area of hybrid renewable energy sources based battery energy storage system (BESS).
the proposed FLC based bi directional DC-DC converter is a promising topology for hybrid energy system.

this research proposes an effective fuzzy logic based battery charging and discharging system in hybrid renewable energy system which is capable to track the maximum power point of the PV and wind sources for maximum energy extraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fuzzy logic based MPPT controller and battery energy management system (BEMS) would be the key factor for the successful operation of the hybrid renewable energy system (HRES).

the proposed FLC based bi directional DC-DC converter for battery management system has the ability to charge and discharge the battery system according to the load demand and the available power from the input sources.
the fuzzy logic based control algorithm for battery management system in hybrid PV/WECS system is a promising solution for the future smart grid applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed FLC based bi directional DC/ DC converter can be used to charge and discharge battery bank based on the load demand and supply.
the fuzzy logic based control algorithm is more efficient and effective compared to the conventional control techniques.
the fuzzy logic controller based battery management system is able to maintain the battery state of charge (SOC) within 90-100% for the different load demand.
